newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Dec 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Dec 24.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Fidel Ramos underwent surgery on Monday to remove a blockage in an artery in the neck but was recuperating well and was eager to get back to work, officials said. (ALL PAPERS)
- Congress approved on Monday a bill appropriating 41 billion pesos for the salary increases of government employees. (ALL PAPERS)
- Communists rebels have declared a 10-day ceasefire against government forces beginning on Christmas Eve. (INQUIRER)

- Fears over the state of President Fidel Ramos' health caused upheavals on the local stock and foreign exchange markets on Monday, although most were contained before trading sessions closed. (TODAY)
- The Philippines' unemployment rate in October 1996 dropped to 7.4 percent compared with 8.4 percent in the same month last year, the National Statistics Office said. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- Local oil exploration companies plan to drill at least nine "wild cat" wells next year. (BUSINESS DAILY)
